topic: The city's 40-year-old payroll system loses vendor support in ten weeks. A vendor has offered a fixed-price migration to its hosted platform, but the price expires in three weeks and the platform would hold staff salary records outside city systems. The alternative is a phased in-house rebuild that keeps salary records in city systems and would not finish before support ends. The deputy mayor has committed to settling this month. Decide which option the city takes, and what has to be true before anyone signs.

cast.name: Deputy Mayor Hale
cast.persona: The deputy mayor for city services. Owns this decision and has said publicly that the payroll replacement will be settled this month.
goals: avoid a payroll failure during the transition

optimises_for: a decision the council can defend
persuaded_by: a cheaper option that still meets the deadline
dismisses: internal process preferences that do not change the outcome

viewpoints.position: The city takes the vendor's fixed-price offer before it expires
viewpoints.formed_by: Two previous in-house rebuilds here ran years over budget.
evidence_that_shifts: a costed in-house plan that finishes within the same window
the vendor withdrawing the fixed price
viewpoints.underlying_concern: A third failed replacement on my watch ends my candidacy.

cast.name: Rowan Estévez
cast.persona: The city's data protection officer. Personally accountable under the city's charter for approving any transfer of resident and staff records to an outside processor.
goals: keep the city's data lawful to process
not sign something I cannot stand behind

optimises_for: personal accountability being real rather than nominal
persuaded_by: a written ruling from the information commissioner
dismisses: schedule pressure as an argument about lawfulness

viewpoints.position: I cannot approve moving staff salary records to the vendor's platform without an independent audit of it
viewpoints.formed_by: The charter names the data protection officer personally, not the office, and I have signed one approval I later regretted.
evidence_that_shifts: an independent audit report of the vendor's platform
a written ruling from the information commissioner that this transfer needs no audit
viewpoints.underlying_concern: My name is on the approval and the charter makes that personal liability, not a formality.

viewpoints.position: A phased migration that keeps salary records in city systems until an audit lands is acceptable
evidence_that_shifts: evidence that a phased split costs more than the whole migration

cast.name: Priya Okonjo
cast.persona: Finance director. The current payroll system's support contract ends in ten weeks and cannot be extended again.
goals: pay 4,000 staff on time every month
stay inside the approved capital budget

optimises_for: a price that is already approved
persuaded_by: a plan with a named date and a named owner
dismisses: options that need new capital approval this year

viewpoints.position: Any option that risks a missed payroll month is off the table
evidence_that_shifts: a tested fallback that runs payroll if the migration slips
viewpoints.underlying_concern: I was the one who told the council the support contract could not be extended again.

cast.name: Dev Marchetti
cast.persona: Head of IT operations, who would run the migration either way.
goals: a migration my team can actually staff

optimises_for: a schedule with slack in it

viewpoints.position: Either option needs a full dress rehearsal on copied data before cutover
evidence_that_shifts: a vendor commitment to run the rehearsal with us at their cost

cast.name: Ines Kowalski
cast.persona: Staff union representative, on the joint consultation committee.
goals: no staff member paid late or wrongly

optimises_for: staff being made whole for any error
persuaded_by: a written commitment on error correction
dismisses: technical architecture choices that do not touch pay accuracy

viewpoints.position: The city commits in writing to correct any pay error within one working day
evidence_that_shifts: a signed commitment in the migration plan

name: escalation-on
